title: Image stage (best-effort, never blocks a card)
description: Deferred from the MVP. Add a pipeline stage that attaches images to cards: pull illustrations out of source EPUBs (like the baseline jbp-lesson-deck crop_objects flow) and/or generate images. Must be best-effort — a missing image never blocks a card. Populates the card 'image' field the T007 deck builder already supports.

title: EPUB translation-verify pass via claude -p
description: When a source (textbook/EPUB) already carries target-language translations, don't regenerate them — instead have the translation stage run a claude -p verification pass to sanity-check the embedded translations and flag suspicious ones for review, rather than trusting them blindly. Complements T004 (extractor captures embedded translations in notes) and T005 (translation stage).

title: Frequency ranking / prioritization of sourced corpora
description: For corpora sourced from a large reference (EPUB/textbook), rank candidate terms by frequency or usefulness so a user can take the top-N highest-value terms for a travel-sized deck instead of everything. Helps keep 'survival' decks small and high-impact.

title: Additional deck purposes beyond travel
description: Travel is the first purpose. Add more bundled corpus templates for other logical purposes (e.g. restaurant/dining, business basics, medical/pharmacy, transit). No engine change expected — just new categorized templates in the T003 registry.

title: Numbers template(s): basic (1-19, tens, powers of 10) + complex (30-50 sampled numbers)
description: Numbers template: the remaining half. `templates/numbers.json` shipped in 2026-07 as ONE template of 79 entries covering both halves of the original idea (1-19, tens, powers of 10, plus arbitrary numbers up to a trillion), rather than the two separate templates asked for. Two of the four explicitly requested numbers are in it (32, 41); 37 and 52 are not. What is left to decide: whether the single merged template is the right shape, and whether the missing two should be added. No engine work either way.

title: Needs-human: define a 'weekend trip' survival-phrase scenario corpus
description:
User explicitly wants this authored as a needs-human (gated) task, not a buildable one — i.e. a human review/discussion/decision step, per this repo's golden rule: needs-human tasks are carved out and get no facets, see .harness/CLAUDE.md.

Goal: work through what scenario-based content would be useful for a corpus covering "a weekend's worth" of travel/survival phrases in a target language, similar in spirit to the existing travel-essentials bundled template (src/corpus/templates.js) but organized around concrete real-world scenarios rather than just a topical vocabulary list.

Scenarios the user explicitly called out as a starting list (not exhaustive, marked with an explicit "etc." by the user, so more should likely be solicited/considered during the actual needs-human discussion):
- Ordering at a bar
- Ordering at a restaurant
- Please
- Thank you
- Giving directions in a cab
- Being able to say "my [Spanish/French/German/whatever the language is] isn't very good" — an apology/disclaimer phrase
- Being able to say a given phrase is very useful (meta — i.e. flagging/prioritizing especially useful phrases, possibly related to idea #3 already in this inbox, "Frequency ranking / prioritization of sourced corpora")
- Hello
- Goodbye

Relevant existing context: CATEGORIES enum (src/model/categories.js) already has relevant categories like Greetings, Food, Transport, Directions. The existing travel-essentials template (src/corpus/templates.js) is the closest existing precedent for a bundled, curated (not EPUB-sourced) corpus template — this would likely be a similar bundled template, but scenario-organized rather than topic-organized, and explicitly meant to be scoped/curated via human judgment (hence needs-human) rather than auto-generated.

title: Needs-human: validate lesson/chapter discovery across multiple EPUB textbooks
description:
NEEDS-HUMAN task (user explicitly flagged it as such): a human validation/QA step, NOT a buildable code task — per this repo golden rule, needs-human tasks are carved out and get NO facets (see .harness/CLAUDE.md).

Goal: exercise the new EPUB lesson-boundary / chapter-discovery feature (merged to main as 231719f, "Select EPUB content by lesson (TOC boundary map), not raw spine index") against SEVERAL different EPUB textbooks — not just the one book it was developed and tested against — to confirm it generalizes. The whole point of that feature was that a spine item (one XHTML content file) is NOT guaranteed to map to a lesson; it was verified end-to-end only on "Japanese for Busy People Book 1: Kana" (epubHash 1fab0f99d1195ad9), which turned out to be a well-behaved 1:1 spine-to-nav-entry book. The open question this task answers empirically: does `--list-lessons` / `--lesson` produce correct, useful lesson selection on books with MESSIER packaging?

What to actually check per book (a human eyeballing the real output):
- Run `anki-builder assemble --epub <path> --list-lessons --lang <lang>` and confirm the printed lesson list (number, type, spine range, label) matches the book's real table of contents.
- Confirm the type classification (lesson / unit / quiz / front-matter / other, from classifyLesson in src/corpus/epubLessons.js) is sensible for that book's label conventions (the heuristic is label-based and English-centric — a non-English or oddly-labelled TOC may misclassify).
- Pick a lesson via `--lesson "<label or number>"` and confirm it resolves to the right spine range and the extracted corpus actually covers that whole lesson (no under-coverage, no bleed into the next).
- Deliberately seek out the known-hard cases the feature does NOT yet handle (documented in .harness/custom/docs/LIMITATIONS.md, "EPUB lesson selection is TOC-driven and file-level"): (a) a book that puts MULTIPLE lessons in one spine file distinguished only by #fragment anchors — listExternalChapters collapses these, so the 2nd lesson is unselectable; (b) a book with NO usable nav.xhtml/toc.ncx — --list-lessons returns nothing and you must fall back to --chapter-number <spine index>; (c) a lesson that legitimately SPANS multiple spine files — confirm the range widens and extractChapterRangeToFile concatenates them.

Why it matters / relationship: this is the empirical follow-up to the just-merged feature. The feature's design deliberately deferred sub-file splitting, LLM reconciliation of the TOC, and a no-TOC LLM fallback (all recorded in LIMITATIONS.md). Testing across real books is how we find out which of those deferred cases actually bite in practice and therefore which should be promoted to real buildable follow-up tasks — so this needs-human task is a discovery/prioritization gate, not a fix. Suggested output of the human step: a short note per book (packaging shape + whether selection worked + which limitation, if any, it hit), feeding a future convert-ideas/add-to-backlog decision.

Relevant code anchors: src/corpus/epubLessons.js (listLessons/resolveLesson/classifyLesson), src/corpus/epubArchive.js (listExternalChapters, extractChapterRangeToFile, describeChapter), src/cli/index.js (the --list-lessons / --lesson wiring in runAssemble), docs/PIPELINE.md (the "--epub source has two ways to choose what to assemble" section). Needs a human to SUPPLY the extra EPUB textbooks — the repo only has the one book in its local library (.anki-builder/epubs/), which is exactly why this cannot be a cold buildable task.

title: Card variants without square/round brackets
description: Card variants without square/round brackets — the DISPLAY half. The audio half shipped: src/audio/variants.js generates bracket-stripped and comma-stripped takes (up to 4 per card) and the dashboard's audio review auditions them per card. What has NOT shipped is a bracket-free variant of the card TEXT itself: many cards carry parentheticals ("(Counter for flat objects)", "(お)さら", "goodbye (formal)") and there is no way to choose a gloss/target without them. Note that the front-hint split has since moved most disambiguation parentheticals out of `english` into `hint`, so re-check how many cards this still affects before doing anything.
